item.title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for July 31
item.description: Oil steadied at the end of a volatile week, with prices on track for the biggest monthly gain since March as the US-Iran war escalated.

item.title: Amazon Got $600 Million Tariff Refund, Some for Shoppers
item.description: Amazon.com Inc. says it received about $600 million in tariff refunds during the second quarter and pledged to automatically issue reimbursements to consumers under a “limited set of circumstances.”

item.title: Japan PM Takaichi Faces Biggest Test Yet as Yen Sinks, Approval Ratings Drop
item.description: Japan’s prime minister is hitting a rough patch after winning the nation’s biggest electoral mandate since World War II.

item.title: Carvana Bears Reap $500 Million as Stock Sinks on Profit Miss
item.description: The slump in the shares of online used-car dealer Carvana Co. on Thursday is creating a potential windfall for investors who have been bearish on the stock.

item.title: Coinbase Posts Loss as Revenue Drops for Another Quarter
item.description: Coinbase Global Inc. reported a third consecutive quarterly decline in revenue, showing once again how a cooling crypto market can pressure even one of the industry’s most diversified exchanges.

item.title: Apple Slides After Supply Shortages Hurt Its Sales Forecast
item.description: Apple Inc. tumbled in late trading after component shortages weighed on the company’s sales forecast, signaling that industrywide supply constraints are taking a bigger toll than anticipated.

item.title: Churchill Downs Shares Fall on Plans to Sell Casinos, Keep Derby
item.description: Churchill Downs Inc. shares tumbled nearly 7% on Thursday to their lowest level in six years after the company announced plans to sell nine of its regional casinos and focus on its horseracing properties.

item.title: Strategy Shores Up Liquidity as Faithful Wait on Rebound
item.description: After roiling crypto markets with a sweeping overhaul of the financing model underpinning Strategy Inc.’s Bitcoin buying blueprint, Michael Saylor has investors wondering what’s next while reporting another multibillion loss tied to the declining value of the cryptocurrency accumulator’s holdings.

item.title: Roblox Users Miss Estimates on Impact of Safety Measures
item.description: Roblox Corp. reported second-quarter daily active users that missed analysts’ expectations, reflecting the ongoing impact of new child-safety measures.

item.title: Amazon Reports Fifth Straight Quarter of Cloud Sales Growth
item.description: Amazon.com Inc. reported cloud-computing revenue that accelerated for the fifth straight quarter, easing investors’ concerns that the company won’t produce a return on its spending to meet booming demand for artificial intelligence.

item.title: Reddit Projects Strong Sales, But No New AI Deals
item.description: Reddit Inc. projected revenue in the current quarter revenue that beat Wall Street estimates, but shares fell after the social media company failed to announce any new data licensing agreements.

item.title: Fitch’s Private Credit Default Rate Hit Record in Second Quarter
item.description: The default rate across 1,300 US private debt borrowers tracked by Fitch Ratings rose to a record high in the second quarter, according to a report released Thursday.

item.title: Weak Yen Offers Toyota an Earnings Respite From Tariffs, War
item.description: The yen’s slide to a 40-year low may be causing headaches for Japanese policymakers, but exporters such as Toyota Motor Corp. are set to reap an earnings boon, offering a much-needed respite from US tariffs, surging oil prices and strained supply chains.

item.title: Warsh Hints at New Inflation Roadmap, Stoking Investor Angst
item.description: Tucked into Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh’s eventful press conference on Wednesday was a suggestion the US central bank could shift its approach to assessing inflation — a remark that’s sowing angst among some investors.

item.title: Bolivia Central Bank to Buy, Sell Dollars to Stabilize FX Rate
item.description: Bolivia’s central bank will step into the foreign exchange market to stabilize the currency after it sank 22% since the country adopted a flexible FX regime a month ago.

item.title: How Fed Chief Kevin Warsh Baffled Markets on Inflation
item.description: What the Fed chief said and didn’t say after this week’s rate meeting.

item.title: Banks Line Up $15 Billion of Debt for Anthropic With Google Aid
item.description: Banks led by Morgan Stanley are in talks to line up $15 billion of debt for an Anthropic PBC data-center project in Texas, backstopped by Alphabet Inc.’s Google, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: US Refiners See Billions in Profits From Global Fuel Crunch
item.description: US refiners running all-out to meet a global fuel shortage posted some of their most profitable quarters ever, as years of domestic refinery closures and wars tightened supplies worldwide.

item.title: Podcasters Are Building Businesses Off Free TV Channels
item.description: For podcasters delving into video programming, YouTube isn’t the only game in town

item.title: Oil Billionaire Hamm Seeks to Expand in Argentina’s Shale Patch
item.description: US shale pioneer Harold Hamm is moving to expand his footprint in Argentina’s Vaca Muerta oil basin, home to the world’s fastest-growing shale boom, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: DeepSeek Is Developing Massive AI Data Center in Inner Mongolia
item.description: China’s DeepSeek is planning a massive artificial-intelligence data center in Inner Mongolia, according to people familiar with the matter, an ambitious move in computing infrastructure from the startup that’s shown it can compete with the leading AI models of Silicon Valley.

item.title: UK’s FCA to Publish Daily Stock-Trading Data Starting Friday
item.description: The Financial Conduct Authority, the UK’s markets regulator, plans to publish a daily summary of trading in the country’s shares starting Friday, part of its effort to increase transparency, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Judge Voices Doubt US Has Justified Its Ban on Anthropic AI
item.description: A judge said the Trump administration has not presented enough evidence “really justifying” its decision to ban the federal government from using artificial intelligence technology from Anthropic PBC by designating the company as a threat to the supply chain.

item.title: Qualcomm CEO Says the Smartphone Market Will Stay ‘Suppressed’
item.description: Qualcomm Inc. Chief Executive Officer Cristiano Amon said demand for smartphones remains strong, but the growing costs of making the devices are keeping the market down.

item.title: Wall Street’s Record Fed Funds Short Unravels After Rates Held
item.description: A raft of wagers placed ahead of the Federal Reserve’s policy decision to hedge the possibility of an interest-rate hike are unraveling after officials kept rates unchanged.

item.title: Exelon (EXC) Slashes AI Data Center Pipeline, Weeds Out Speculative Projects
item.description: Exelon Corp. slashed its forecast for new data center projects amid mounting opposition across the US to AI facilities.

item.title: Goldman Says Microsoft Shows Wall Street How AI Bet Pays Off
item.description: Microsoft Corp. is giving investors clearer signs that it has multiple ways to turn its artificial-intelligence investment into revenue, Goldman Sachs Group Inc. analyst Gabriela Borges said, as the shares surged the most in almost 18 years.

item.title: Omers Hires CAAT’s Buzanis to Lead Private Equity Funds Business
item.description: Ontario Municipal Employees Retirement System hired a longtime executive from CAAT Pension Plan to help build its private equity funds strategy as it makes such investing a more central part of its buyout business.

item.title: Xerox Taps Tariffs Refund Claim to Help Address Looming Debt
item.description: Xerox Holdings Corp. sold tariff refund claims at a discount to raise cash and reduce its debt load last quarter, as it looks to address its hefty maturities over the next three years.
